config.title: CSS architecture

intro.title: CSS architecture
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, responsive webpage to learn the fundamentals of CSS architecture. You will apply core concepts like separation of concerns, maintainability, and scalability by organizing your styles effectively. The main technologies involved are HTML for structure and CSS for styling, using techniques such as semantic class naming and modular CSS. By the end, you'll understand how to structure CSS to keep your code clean and easy to manage as projects grow.
intro.usecase: CSS architecture is essential for maintaining large-scale applications like e-commerce platforms, where consistent styling must be applied across thousands of product cards, navigation menus, and checkout forms. In enterprise dashboards, a well-structured CSS system ensures that data tables, charts, and control panels remain visually cohesive as new features are added. Developers rely on CSS architecture patterns like BEM or utility-first approaches to efficiently manage design systems in complex applications like social media feeds or admin interfaces, where reusable components prevent styling conflicts and speed up development.

objectives: Apply CSS custom properties to create a consistent design system
Construct modular CSS components with BEM naming conventions
Configure a CSS architecture that separates base, layout, and component styles
Implement responsive design patterns using CSS Grid and Flexbox
Integrate CSS methodologies to maintain scalable and maintainable code
Manipulate CSS specificity to control style precedence and avoid conflicts
Initialize a CSS architecture that supports theming and design tokens

steps.title: Create the main CSS file and import it
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file named 'styles.css' and import it into your main JavaScript file using import './styles.css'
steps.hint: In your project, create a file called styles.css in the same directory as your JavaScript file. Then, in your JavaScript file, add an import statement at the top to bring in the CSS.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing a CSS file
import './custom-styles.css';
steps.seedCode:
// Import the CSS file here

// Your JavaScript code will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a styles.css file created and imported into your JavaScript file, establishing the foundation for CSS architecture.
successCriteria: The styles.css file exists and is imported using import './styles.css' at the top of the JavaScript file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both created the styles.css file and imported it using import './styles.css'.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a CSS file named styles.css and import it into your JavaScript file with import './styles.css'.

steps.title: Define CSS custom properties (CSS variables)
steps.instruction: In your styles.css file, define CSS custom properties (variables) for colors, spacing, and typography inside the :root selector.
steps.hint: The :root selector targets the highest-level element (like <html>). Define variables using --variable-name: value; syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: The styles.css file will contain a :root selector with at least one CSS custom property defined for colors, spacing, or typography.
successCriteria: The :root selector contains custom properties (variables) for colors, spacing, and/or typography using the --variable-name: value; syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining CSS custom properties, but make sure they're inside the :root selector and use the correct --variable-name: value; syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file doesn't contain the expected custom properties in the :root selector. Review the syntax: :root { --variable-name: value; }

steps.title: Create a CSS reset or normalize styles
steps.instruction: Add CSS reset rules to remove default browser styling and establish consistent baseline styles. Start by adding a rule that sets margin and padding to 0 for all elements.
steps.hint: Use the universal selector (*) to target all elements and set margin and padding to 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will have a reset rule that removes default margins and padding from all elements, creating a consistent baseline for styling.
successCriteria: A CSS rule using the universal selector (*) is added with margin: 0 and padding: 0 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a CSS rule, but make sure it uses the universal selector (*) and sets both margin and padding to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS reset rule is missing or incorrect. Add a rule with the universal selector (*) that sets margin and padding to 0.

steps.title: Define base element styles
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the body element using the CSS variables defined earlier. Set the background color, text color, font family, and margin.
steps.hint: Use the :root CSS variables you created in step 2. For example, you can set background-color: var(--color-background); and color: var(--color-text);
steps.expectedOutcome: The body element will have consistent styling using your CSS variables for colors and typography.
successCriteria: The body selector has CSS rules that use at least two CSS variables (e.g., --color-background, --color-text) and sets background-color, color, font-family, and margin properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started styling the body, but make sure you're using your CSS variables (like var(--color-background)) and include all the required properties: background-color, color, font-family, and margin.
steps.feedbackWrong: The body element styling is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the CSS variables you defined earlier and set the required properties for consistent base styling.

steps.title: Create utility classes
steps.instruction: Define a utility class for margin by adding a CSS rule for `.m-1` that sets `margin: 1rem`.
steps.hint: Add a CSS rule starting with `.m-1` and inside the curly braces set the margin property to 1rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS utility class `.m-1` is defined with `margin: 1rem`.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for `.m-1` with `margin: 1rem`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the utility class, but check that the property and value are exactly `margin: 1rem`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The utility class wasn't defined correctly. Make sure you create a rule for `.m-1` with `margin: 1rem`.

steps.title: Define component styles
steps.instruction: Create a component style block for a button component using BEM naming convention. Add a CSS rule for the block class `.button` with padding, border, and background color.
steps.hint: Start by writing a CSS rule for `.button` with properties like padding, border, and background-color. Use the CSS variables defined earlier for colors if needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: A `.button` CSS rule is added with padding, border, and background color properties.
successCriteria: The `.button` class is defined with at least padding, border, and background-color properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the `.button` rule, but it's missing some required properties. Make sure to include padding, border, and background-color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The `.button` component style block is not properly defined. Check that you've written a CSS rule for `.button` with the required properties.

steps.title: Implement layout classes
steps.instruction: Define a layout class for a responsive container that centers content and adds horizontal padding.
steps.hint: Create a CSS class named .container with max-width, margin auto, and padding properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container class is added to the CSS file with properties for responsive centering and padding.
successCriteria: The .container class is defined with max-width, margin: auto, and padding properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a layout class, but check if it includes all required properties: max-width, margin auto, and padding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The layout class is missing or incomplete. Try defining a .container class with responsive layout properties.

steps.title: Create responsive design breakpoints
steps.instruction: Add a media query for mobile screens (max-width: 768px) that adjusts the .button component's padding and font-size.
steps.expectedOutcome: A media query is added that modifies the .button styles for screens up to 768px wide.
successCriteria: The code includes @media (max-width: 768px) with .button rules adjusting padding and font-size.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a media query, but make sure it targets .button and adjusts both padding and font-size.
steps.feedbackWrong: The responsive breakpoint is missing or incorrect. Check the syntax and ensure it modifies .button for max-width: 768px.

steps.title: Organize CSS with comments and sections
steps.instruction: Add descriptive comments above each major section in your CSS file to clearly separate and document the purpose of each group of styles.
steps.hint: Use CSS comments (/* comment */) to label sections like custom properties, reset, base styles, utilities, components, layout, and responsive breakpoints.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your CSS file will have clear, labeled sections with comments that make the code organization easy to understand.
successCriteria: Each major section (custom properties, reset, base styles, utilities, components, layout, responsive) has a descriptive comment above it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some comments, but make sure each major section (custom properties, reset, base styles, utilities, components, layout, responsive) has its own descriptive comment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file still lacks clear section comments. Add comments above each major group of styles to organize the code.

steps.title: Test the CSS architecture with sample HTML
steps.instruction: Create a sample HTML structure that uses all the CSS architecture components (variables, utilities, components, layouts) to test the complete system.
steps.hint: Add a <div> with classes that apply your CSS variables, utilities, component styles, and layout classes. Include elements like buttons and text to see the styles in action.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: HTML structure using CSS classes

steps.expectedOutcome: A complete HTML structure that demonstrates how all CSS architecture components work together, with visible styling applied through classes.
successCriteria: The HTML structure includes at least one element using CSS variables, one utility class, one component class, and one layout class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Your HTML structure is partially complete. Make sure it uses CSS variables, utilities, components, and layouts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure doesn't yet test the CSS architecture. Try adding elements with classes that apply your styles.
